scenes.narration: Can an AI Agent stay on track across context windows? Use a handoff.
scenes.headline: AI Agent across context windows

scenes.narration: Anthropic studied this problem in a long-running coding setup. Their useful conclusion is simple: do not ask a fresh session to rediscover the whole project before it can help.
scenes.headline: Anthropic tested a long-running setup

scenes.narration: Without a working floor, an Agent can restart by guessing, repeat already-finished work, or mistake a half-built feature for a completed task. That burns time and quietly raises risk.
scenes.headline: Restarts burn time and raise risk
scenes.coreLabel: Restarts burn time and raise risk

scenes.narration: The reusable tool in this episode is a Long-Running AI Agent Progress & Handoff Card. It turns a vague continuation request into a small, inspectable next move.
scenes.headline: A small handoff directs the next session
scenes.coreLabel: A small handoff directs the next session

scenes.narration: We will separate the reset problem, the minimum starting state, the size of a good next move, the handoff itself, and the evidence required before progress is claimed.
scenes.headline: The five-part continuity plan

scenes.narration: This video is packed with practical, high-value insights to help you get better at using AI. It's a longer one, so follow Tiny Agent and save it so you don't lose it.
scenes.headline: Save this progress system for later
scenes.coreLabel: Save this progress system for later

scenes.narration: A long task does not become continuous just because the Agent has a loop. Each context window is a new session with incomplete memory of what happened before.
scenes.headline: Chapter 1: The Reset Problem
scenes.coreLabel: Each context window is a new session with incomplete

scenes.narration: That reset creates two costly failure modes. The Agent can attempt too much at once, or it can see partial progress and declare the entire job finished.
scenes.headline: Too much work or premature completion
scenes.coreLabel: Too much work or premature completion

scenes.narration: Compaction can preserve some context, but it is not a substitute for a durable work state. A new session still needs to know what matters now.
scenes.headline: New sessions need the current state
scenes.coreLabel: New sessions need the current state

scenes.narration: Treat the handoff as an interface, not as a diary. It should help the next Agent choose a safe next action without rereading every past conversation.
scenes.headline: Choose a safe next action

scenes.narration: Do not ask what the last session discussed. Ask what is true in the environment, what remains unproven, and what should happen next.
scenes.headline: Inspect state, uncertainty, and next steps
scenes.coreLabel: Inspect state, uncertainty, and next steps

scenes.narration: A reset becomes manageable when the project keeps a small source of truth outside the context window.
scenes.headline: Keep state outside the window

scenes.narration: Chapter recap. First, a context window reset can erase practical working state.
scenes.headline: A reset can erase working state
scenes.recapDisplayText: A reset can erase working state
scenes.coreLabel: A reset can erase working state

scenes.narration: Second, partial work can trigger either repeated effort or premature completion.
scenes.headline: Avoid repeats and premature claims
scenes.recapDisplayText: Partial work invites repeats or premature claims
scenes.coreLabel: Partial work invites repeats or premature claims

scenes.narration: Third, the next session needs an actionable state, not a transcript.
scenes.headline: Actionable state beats a transcript

scenes.narration: Start with a working floor before asking an AI Agent to add a feature. The floor is the smallest verified state from which new work is safe.
scenes.headline: Chapter 2: Build a Working Floor
scenes.coreLabel: The floor is the smallest verified state from which

scenes.narration: For software work, that usually includes a runnable environment, a feature list, a progress record, and a quick end-to-end check. Other domains need equivalent anchors.
scenes.headline: Use equivalent anchors in other domains
scenes.coreLabel: Use equivalent anchors in other domains

scenes.narration: The initializer has a distinct job: make future sessions less dependent on inference. It prepares the map before anyone starts driving.
scenes.headline: Map the work before driving

scenes.narration: Keep requirements in a structure that makes completion visible. A feature is not complete because it sounds finished; it is complete when its observable behavior passes.
scenes.headline: A feature needs real verification

scenes.narration: Also record the current constraints: accepted inputs, forbidden changes, known failures, and the evidence a reviewer will need.
scenes.headline: Make requirements easy to inspect

scenes.narration: A stable floor reduces the temptation to rebuild the foundation in every session.
scenes.headline: Prepare the next session

scenes.narration: Chapter recap. First, create a minimal verified starting environment.
scenes.headline: Verify a minimal working floor

scenes.narration: Second, make requirements and current constraints easy to inspect.
scenes.headline: Expose requirements and constraints

scenes.narration: Third, treat the initializer as setup for future sessions, not as one-shot delivery.
scenes.headline: Prepare future sessions

scenes.narration: Once the floor exists, shrink the next move. A long-running AI Agent should advance one meaningful unit instead of trying to finish the whole project in one pass.
scenes.headline: Chapter 3: Shrink the Next Move
scenes.coreLabel: A long-running AI Agent should advance one meaningfu

scenes.narration: Choose a unit that has a clear boundary: one feature, one failure to reproduce, one data check, or one reviewable decision. It should fit inside the available context.
scenes.headline: Fit the next move in context
scenes.coreLabel: Fit the next move in context

scenes.narration: A small move still needs a result. The Agent should change a real state, run the relevant verification, and say what that verification did and did not prove.
scenes.headline: Change, test, then record

scenes.narration: This is not slow for its own sake. Small completed units avoid the expensive recovery work caused by abandoned half-implementations.
scenes.headline: Small units reduce recovery cost

scenes.narration: When a request is too large, split by a user-observable outcome rather than by arbitrary files or token counts.
scenes.headline: Tie work to a verification signal
scenes.coreLabel: Tie work to a verification signal

scenes.narration: The progress card should name one next move, its success signal, and its stop condition.
scenes.headline: Split work by observable outcome

scenes.narration: Chapter recap. First, give each session one bounded meaningful objective.
scenes.headline: Choose one bounded objective

scenes.narration: Second, connect that objective to a real verification signal.
scenes.headline: Attach a real success signal

scenes.narration: Third, split oversized work by observable outcome, not by convenience.
scenes.headline: Split by observable outcome

scenes.narration: A useful handoff answers four questions fast: what changed, what is verified, what is uncertain, and what is the next smallest safe action.
scenes.headline: Chapter 4: Write the Handoff

scenes.narration: Write decisions and evidence beside each other. A choice is usable when it names the browser evidence that passed and the alternative that failed.
scenes.headline: Evidence makes a decision usable

scenes.narration: Leave paths to the source of truth, not a copied wall of context. The next Agent can inspect the feature list, progress note, tests, or artifacts on demand.
scenes.headline: Link the feature list and progress
scenes.coreLabel: Link the feature list and progress

scenes.narration: Keep the environment clean enough for another person or Agent to begin immediately. Hidden breakage is not progress merely because a diff exists.
scenes.headline: A diff is not progress by itself
scenes.coreLabel: A diff is not progress by itself

scenes.narration: A good handoff also names a boundary: do not change this integration, do not claim this metric, or wait for this external approval.
scenes.headline: Record decisions with evidence

scenes.narration: That boundary is how you preserve human judgment when the Agent continues independently.
scenes.headline: Link sources, not context

scenes.narration: Chapter recap. First, record changes, evidence, uncertainty, and the next move.
scenes.headline: Record evidence with decisions

scenes.narration: Second, link to inspectable sources instead of copying all context.
scenes.headline: Link to inspectable sources

scenes.narration: Third, make constraints explicit so the next Agent does not overreach.
scenes.headline: Make boundaries explicit

scenes.narration: Before an AI Agent marks progress complete, verify the claimed outcome at the level the user will experience. A unit test alone may not prove an end-to-end feature works.
scenes.headline: Chapter 5: Verify Before Advance
scenes.coreLabel: A unit test alone may not prove an end-to-end featur

scenes.narration: The source article describes better results when Agents were explicitly prompted to use browser automation for end-to-end checks in a web-app setting.
scenes.headline: Verify user-visible outcomes

scenes.narration: Use the narrowest sufficient check first, then add a realistic workflow check when the claim affects an interface, integration, or delivery.
scenes.headline: Evidence before a completion claim

scenes.narration: Update the progress card only after the evidence exists. A pass flag is an output of verification, not a substitute for it.
scenes.headline: A pass flag is not the proof
scenes.coreLabel: A pass flag is not the proof

scenes.narration: When verification fails, preserve the failure, the reproduction path, and the smallest next diagnostic step. That turns a reset into a focused continuation.
scenes.headline: Turn resets into focused continuations

scenes.narration: This is also the human gate: people decide whether the evidence is enough for the consequence at stake.
scenes.headline: Failures become next diagnostics

scenes.narration: Chapter recap. First, verify outcomes at the level users actually experience.
scenes.headline: Check user-visible outcomes

scenes.narration: Second, record evidence before changing a task to complete.
scenes.headline: Evidence comes before completion

scenes.narration: Third, turn failures into precise next diagnostics rather than vague retries.
scenes.headline: Failures become next diagnostics

scenes.narration: Long-running AI Agents need continuity by design, not by optimism.
scenes.headline: A handoff makes continuity visible

scenes.narration: First, establish a working floor with a runnable environment, clear requirements, and a fast reality check.
scenes.headline: Build a verified working floor

scenes.narration: Second, make one bounded move at a time and verify its observable result.
scenes.headline: Choose a bounded next move

scenes.narration: Third, leave a handoff that states changes, evidence, uncertainty, boundaries, and the next safe action.
scenes.headline: Write an evidence-backed handoff

scenes.narration: Use the Long-Running AI Agent Progress & Handoff Card whenever work must cross sessions, people, or context windows.
scenes.headline: Verify before claiming progress

scenes.narration: The practical test is simple: could a fresh Agent begin useful work without guessing what the last one meant?
scenes.headline: Keep the next session moving
